title: Grade 4 Science — Fri, Jun 20
description: Skeletal System — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — full system
subject: science

questions.question: How many bones does an adult human have?
questions.explanation: An adult human body has 206 bones.

questions.question: Which bones protect the heart and lungs?
questions.explanation: The ribcage (12 pairs of ribs and the sternum) protects the heart and lungs.

questions.question: The femur is:
options: The longest bone — the thigh bone
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.

questions.question: Match: Elbow joint → type of joint:
questions.explanation: The elbow is a hinge joint — it bends and straightens in one direction.

questions.question: Match: Shoulder joint → type of joint:
questions.explanation: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint — it moves in all directions.

questions.question: Match: Skull bones → type of joint:
questions.explanation: The skull bones are joined by fixed/immoveable joints (sutures) to protect the brain.

questions.question: Tendons connect:
questions.explanation: Tendons connect muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone.

questions.question: Cartilage at joints acts as:
questions.explanation: Cartilage cushions joints, reducing friction and absorbing shock so bones don't grind together.

questions.question: The heart is made of ___ muscle:
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is unique to the heart. It beats involuntarily and never stops.

questions.question: Walking uses ___ muscles:
questions.explanation: Walking is voluntary — we consciously decide to walk. Skeletal (voluntary) muscles of the legs are used.

questions.question: Muscles only PULL bones. What provides the pulling action?
options: Muscles contract (shorten) and pull via tendons
questions.explanation: Muscles contract (shorten) and the tendons attached to bones transmit the pulling force, causing the bone to move.

questions.question: Which food group is most important for building strong bones?
questions.explanation: Calcium-rich foods build and maintain strong bones. Vitamin D (from sunlight) helps the body absorb calcium.

questions.question: Bone marrow produces:
options: Blood cells (red, white blood cells and platelets)
questions.explanation: Red bone marrow produces blood cells. Red blood cells carry oxygen; white blood cells fight infection; platelets help blood clot.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the skeleton?
questions.explanation: Digestion is not a function of the skeleton. The skeleton supports, protects organs, produces blood cells, and assists movement.

questions.question: WEEK STAR: A child breaks the bone at the thigh. Which bone is injured, and which system does it belong to?
questions.explanation: The thigh bone is the femur, part of the skeletal system. It is the longest bone in the body.
